questions.solution_html:
• Check feasibility – Make sure questions are practical and realistic to answer.
  • Ethical Soundness: The question should not invade privacy or cause harm to
  • participants. OR
  • The FINER Criteria is a useful guideline for developing a good research question. It stands for
  • Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, and Relevant.

  • including formulating objectives, designing data collection methods, selecting samples, collecting

  • maximize reliability.
  • Introduction and conclusion (5 marks)/Explanation for both research design (5 marks)/ Aspects
  • (10 marks)
  • Aspect Explanation
  • Type of Study
  • Descriptive Study: Describes characteristics, behavior, or trends of a
  • group or situation. Diagnostic Study: Describes and also identifies
  • causes or reasons for a problem.
  • Example Descriptive – Studying online shopping behavior .Diagnostic – Finding reasons for employee performance decline after work-from-home.
  • Reporting Findings Present results using charts, graphs, and tables. Summarize conclusions and make recommendations.
  • Measures to Reduce
  • Bias
  • - Use random sampling - Avoid leading questions - Maintain uniform
  • procedures- Conduct pilot tests
  • Ways to Maximize
  • Reliability
  • - Use standardized tools- Ensure consistency in data collection- Double
  • check data accuracy
  • Conclusion A well -structured research design ensures systematic data collection, accurate analysis, reduced bias, and reliable findings.
  • 10a. A researcher wants to study the effect of advertisements on sales of a product. Identify the
  • variables, suggest suitable scales of measurement, and explain which scaling technique you would
  • apply to measure advertisement effectiveness.
  • i) Identification of Variables (6 Marks)
  • • Independent Variable (Cause): Advertisement (the factor whose effect is being studied).
  • This could include factors like type of advertisement, frequency, duration, media used
  • message content, etc.
  • • Dependent Variable (Effect): Sales of the product (the outcome influenced by
  • advertisements; This measures how much the product is sold after the advertising
  • activity.)
  • • Possible Control Variables: Price, distribution, season, brand image, etc. (optional mention
  • for higher accuracy).
  • ii) Scales of Measurement (Explaining the various scales (5 marks) and what the student plans to
  • use in this study (2 marks))
  • Type of
  • Scale Description How it is used in this study (full marks for any one example)
  • Nominal
  • Scale
  • Used for classifying data without
  • any order or numerical value. It
  • simply labels variables.
  • Used to classify types of advertisements
  • (e.g., TV, print, online, social media). Each
  • type is a separate category with no ranking
  • implied.
  • Ordinal
  • Scale
  • Indicates rank order among
  • variables but does not show equal
  • intervals between ranks.
  • Can be used to rank advertisement
  • preference or effectiveness level (e.g., very
  • effective, effective, neutral, less effective
  • not effective).
  • Interval
  • Scale
  • Measures variables where
  • differences between values are
  • meaningful, but there is no true zero
  • point.
  • Can be used in attitude scales like the Likert
  • scale to measure agreement with
  • statements about advertisement
  • effectiveness (e.g., from Strongly Agree to
  • Strongly Disagree).
  • Ratio
  • Scale
  • Has all the properties of interval
  • scale, and also has a true zero point
  • allowing comparison of absolute
  • magnitudes.
  • Used to measure sales figures (in rupees or
  • units sold) or advertisement frequency
  • (number of ads shown). These have
  • meaningful zero points.
